title: epikrisis — how the Eunoia ecosystem is developing
tagline: Evidence and analysis for the repositories of the Eunoia ecosystem
lede: Epikrisis reads the git histories of the **Eunoia ecosystem** — a group of repositories built around one proof calculus — and asks what actually happened: what was built, what stalled, and where a project's own account of itself differs from its tree. Every figure below is derived from commits recorded in advance, so anybody with the checkouts can reproduce it.

highlight.subject: eunoia-ecosystem-s2
highlight.title: Two presidencies, in commits
highlight.blurb: One repository at a time holds an office called the presidency, sets the direction of the shared work for a stretch, and hands it on. **Two stretches have run.** Stretch 2 looks more than twice as busy as Stretch 1 — and it is not: take out the eleven days Stretch 1 carried no commit at all, and the two terms run at the same pace. Forty-nine commits of Stretch 1 fall outside the only census anybody published of it.
